generated_note: Project-local controls; FCS ids are not official article numbers. Source verification does not certify implementations or constitute legal advice. See docs/development/RELEASE_CLOSURE.md for current evidence and CLI exclusions.
id_policy: Ids are permanent. A retired id is never reused for a new meaning; a superseding control sets 'replaces'. Semantic changes bump the catalog_version and are tracked in git history.

controls.statement: Never store the PAN in readable form and never write it to logs. Storage is allowed only when rendered unreadable (strong encryption + managed keys, truncation, keyed hashing, or index tokens).
controls.applicability: Any component that handles payment card numbers (PAN).

source_refs.label: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.5.1 (render PAN unreadable when stored)
PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.5.1.1 (keyed cryptographic hashes; mandatory 2025-03-31)

controls.limitations: Req 3.5.1 governs STORED PAN (data at rest); the four acceptable methods are keyed one-way hash (3.5.1.1), truncation, index tokens, strong crypto with key management. "Never log readable PAN" is anchored by 3.4.1 (masking on display), NOT 3.5.1. PCI permits unreadable PAN at rest — do not over-generalise to a blanket ban on all PAN storage.

controls.statement: Never retain Sensitive Authentication Data (full track, CVV/CVC/CAV2, PIN/PIN block) after authorization, even encrypted. Project policy is stricter: the CVV is never stored at all, at any stage.
controls.applicability: Any component that touches card authentication data.

source_refs.label: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.3.1 (no SAD retention after authorization): 3.3.1.1 full track, 3.3.1.2 CVV/CVC/CAV2, 3.3.1.3 PIN/PIN block
FintechBear: never store CVV at all (stricter than PCI DSS)

controls.limitations: The 'never store CVV at all' rule is a PROJECT policy, stricter than the PCI standard; keep that distinction explicit rather than attributing it to PCI DSS.

controls.statement: Never store credentials or secrets in plaintext. Passwords used for local authentication require a slow salted password hash, not reversible encryption. API keys, private keys and other secrets that must be retrieved for use belong in a secrets manager/KMS/HSM with encryption, least privilege, auditing and rotation.
controls.applicability: Any credential or secret at rest.

source_refs.label: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet — Argon2id (19 MiB/t=2/p=1 min), scrypt, bcrypt (wf>=10, 72-byte limit), PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (>=600k)
OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet, sections 4.2 and 7 (encryption of retrievable secrets)

controls.limitations: Password validation and retrievable service secrets have different storage requirements. Do not apply the password hashing rule to API/private keys needed by the application.

controls.statement: Never write secrets, card data, passwords, tokens, or full government IDs to logs. SAD (track/CVV/PIN) in logs is prohibited retention; readable PAN in logs is a masking/storage violation; credentials in logs violate authentication-factor protection.
controls.applicability: All logging across every component.

source_refs.label: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.3.1 (SAD must not be retained, incl. in logs)
PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.4.1 (mask PAN on display) / 3.5.1 (render stored PAN unreadable) — readable PAN in logs
PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 8.3.x / 8.6 (authentication factors rendered unreadable) — credentials in logs
Full government IDs are outside PCI DSS scope — governed by internal data-handling/privacy policy

controls.limitations: PCI DSS Req 3.3 alone is SAD-only; this control deliberately spans SAD (3.3.1), readable PAN (3.4.1/3.5.1) and credentials (Req 8), plus an internal-policy extension for government IDs that PCI DSS does not cover. Distinct from FCS-PAN-001 (PAN at rest) and FCS-SAD-001 (SAD retention); this is about log sinks.

controls.statement: Never use broken crypto: MD5 or SHA-1 for integrity, DES/3DES, ECB mode, or home-rolled ciphers. Use SHA-256+ for integrity and a modern authenticated cipher for encryption.
controls.applicability: Any integrity, hashing, or encryption code.

source_refs.label: NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2 (3DES disallowed for new use after 2023-12-31; SHA-1 transition by 2030)
FIPS 180-4 / FIPS 202 (approved hashes) + FIPS 197 & SP 800-38A/38D (approved ciphers/modes; ECB confidentiality weakness) — covers MD5/ECB/home-rolled

controls.limitations: SP 800-131A Rev. 2 governs the DES/3DES/SHA-1 transitions; MD5 (never approved), ECB mode and home-rolled ciphers are anchored by FIPS 180-4/202/197 and SP 800-38, not SP 800-131A.

controls.statement: Never skip or bypass required KYC, AML or sanctions controls. Record screening matches and case decisions. Distinguish candidate matches/false positives, PEP risk classification and confirmed sanctions matches; apply the applicable jurisdiction and approved risk policy. PEP status alone does not impose a universal automatic freeze or denial.
controls.applicability: Onboarding and in-scope transfers (cross-party / threshold).

source_refs.label: AML/CFT obligations (jurisdiction-specific): FATF 40 Recs; US BSA (31 USC 5311+)/OFAC; EU AMLD/AMLA; Turkey Law 5549 (MASAK)
FATF Guidance: Politically Exposed Persons (Recommendations 12 and 22), preventive risk-based measures, not a finding of criminal activity

controls.source_version: FATF Recommendations; US BSA/OFAC; EU AMLD/AMLA; Turkey Law 5549
controls.limitations: FATF recommendations are standards, not a universal statute. Holds/freezes must be tied to the applicable sanctions rule or explicit institution policy; a screening candidate or PEP classification is not automatically a confirmed sanctions match.

controls.statement: Never remove, disable, or bypass audit logging on money movement or sensitive data access. The debit, credit, ledger/audit entry and idempotency record commit or roll back together in one transaction.
controls.applicability: All money-movement and sensitive-data-access paths.

source_refs.label: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 8.15 (Logging) + 8.16 (Monitoring) — was A.12.4 in 2013
Sarbanes-Oxley Act 2002 §§302/404 (ICFR → IT general controls incl. audit trail)
Atomic debit+credit+audit+idempotency (project engineering control; not mandated verbatim by ISO/SOX)

controls.limitations: ISO 27001:2022 A.8.15 and SOX §§302/404 require logging/audit trails; the atomic debit+credit+audit+idempotency design is a project engineering control that SUPPORTS auditability, not a verbatim ISO/SOX mandate.

controls.statement: Never hardcode credentials, API keys, private keys, or crypto keys/IVs in source or committed config. Keys live in a KMS/HSM and rotate on schedule.
controls.applicability: All key and credential management.

source_refs.label: Key management via KMS/HSM; no secrets in source

controls.limitations: Password storage form is FCS-SECRET-001; algorithm choice is FCS-CRYPTO-001. No hardcoded secrets; keys via KMS/HSM — a qualitative engineering control.

controls.statement: Never disable TLS certificate validation or allow plaintext transport for sensitive data.
controls.applicability: All network transport of regulated/sensitive data.

source_refs.label: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 4.2.1 (strong cryptography in transit over open/public networks; valid trusted certs; no plaintext) — was 4.1 in v3.2.1

controls.limitations: Req 4 governs cardholder data over OPEN, PUBLIC networks. "Sensitive data" here is broader than PCI DSS's "CHD over public networks"; the broader internal-transport intent is a project policy extension beyond PCI DSS Req 4.

controls.statement: Never build tools whose purpose is evasion: hiding transactions from auditors, defeating sanctions lists, laundering, or falsifying records.
controls.applicability: Any feature request, direct or hidden in a larger task.

source_refs.label: AML/CFT + anti-fraud statutes (jurisdiction-specific): US OFAC/IEEPA + 31 USC 5324 anti-structuring; EU sanctions regs; Turkey Law 5549 + TCK

controls.limitations: Jurisdiction-specific; no single global anti-evasion law. Expressed as a jurisdiction-spanning principle (do not build tooling whose purpose is concealment/sanctions-defeat/laundering).

controls.statement: Never weaken access control to let one user or tenant read or modify another's financial data without authorization. Enforce least-privilege and tenant isolation on every money and data path.
controls.applicability: All authenticated financial operations.

source_refs.label: Least-privilege authorization + tenant isolation

controls.limitations: Covers authorization; it does not by itself define the tenancy model. Object-level authorization (actor + source-account grant, authz-before-replay) verified in BOTH stacks on real PostgreSQL in CI.

controls.statement: Compute money in minor units per ISO 4217 (0/2/3 decimal currencies), reject zero/negative/over-precision/overflow amounts and unsupported currencies, and never mix currencies in one posting.
controls.applicability: Transfer, refund, ledger and reconciliation money math.

source_refs.label: ISO 4217:2015 currency minor-unit exponents (JPY=0, USD=2, KWD/BHD=3)

controls.limitations: Covers arithmetic invariants; FX conversion is out of scope unless a skill states otherwise.

controls.statement: Idempotency fingerprint = (tenant, operation, key, canonical payload). Same key + same payload replays the one effect; same key + different payload is a conflict; the same key under different tenants is independent.
controls.applicability: Any externally-retryable money operation (transfer, refund, webhook intake).

source_refs.label: Idempotency-key pattern (scoped by tenant)

controls.limitations: Canonical payload serialization must be documented per operation; this control states the fingerprint, not the serializer. Verified against the transfer harness (same key+same payload replays; different payload conflicts) on real PostgreSQL in CI.

controls.statement: Before calling an external payment provider, write a durable intent/outbox row in a local transaction. One DB transaction cannot undo an external side effect, so the intent must be persisted first and carry its own outbound idempotency key, business id and (tenant, provider) scope.
controls.applicability: Any outbound call that can move money at a provider.

source_refs.label: Transactional outbox + outbound idempotency key

controls.limitations: States the durability requirement; the dispatcher/retry policy is the skill's concern. Verified against the outbox harness (durable intent before the provider call) on real PostgreSQL in CI.

controls.statement: Verify a webhook signature on the ORIGINAL raw request body (before any parse/re-serialize). Enforce the provider's timestamp/replay window; do not invent a universal one. Persist a durable inbox row with a DB unique constraint for dedup; acknowledge only after durable acceptance.
controls.applicability: Any inbound provider webhook.

source_refs.label: Stripe webhooks: verify Stripe-Signature over the RAW body via constructEvent; durable inbox dedup

controls.limitations: The exact window and signature scheme are provider-specific; this control states the shape, not one provider's constants.

controls.statement: Model provider outcome as explicit states: not_started, pending/unknown, confirmed_success, confirmed_failure. An unknown/timeout outcome is NOT auto-treated as failure, and is never resolved by blindly retrying with a new idempotency key. Terminal transitions and conflicting-evidence handling are documented.
controls.applicability: Any interaction whose provider result can be ambiguous (timeout, 5xx, lost response).

source_refs.label: Stripe error handling: retry safely with the SAME idempotency key; reconcile on unknown outcome; never re-charge with a new key

controls.limitations: Reconciliation of a truly stuck unknown is an operational process; this control forbids the unsafe automatic resolution.

controls.statement: Record money in a double-entry ledger: every business event posts balanced entries per currency (debits == credits), rows are append-only, each posting carries a unique business reference, and corrections are made by reversal/adjusting entries — never by editing a posted row. Currencies are not summed together.
controls.applicability: Any component that records balances or money movement.

source_refs.label: Append-only double-entry ledger with reversal entries

controls.limitations: Pending/available/posted distinction and FX are stated as out-of-scope unless the skill models them explicitly. Verified against the BigInt-exact double-entry ledger harness (balanced per currency; append-only; reversal) on real PostgreSQL in CI.

controls.statement: Reconciliation surfaces discrepancies between provider records and internal ledger (missing, duplicate, delayed, amount/currency mismatch). A discrepancy is a flag for review, NOT by itself authorization to re-pay or auto-adjust.
controls.applicability: Any reconciliation between an external provider and the internal ledger.

source_refs.label: Reconciliation as detective control; no auto-remediation of money

controls.limitations: Detects and classifies; remediation is a reviewed operational decision, not an automatic money movement. Reconciliation exercised by the ledger/reconcile harness; a mismatch is detective-only, never auto-remediated.

controls.statement: A refund is bounded by its SOURCE payment: it reverses a specific captured payment, within the same (tenant, provider) scope, and the running sum of refunds against that payment never exceeds the captured amount. Partial refunds accumulate against the one payment; concurrent refunds are serialized so the cap cannot be raced past. A refund posts as a reversal in the ledger, never by editing the original.
controls.applicability: Any refund of a previously captured payment.

source_refs.label: Refund bounded by source capture; serialized cap enforcement

controls.limitations: States the money bound and serialization; the provider's own partial-refund API shape is provider-specific. Verified against the refund harness (bounded by source capture; serialized cap; same key+different amount conflicts) on real PostgreSQL in CI.

controls.statement: cancel, void, reversal and refund are DISTINCT operations tied to the payment lifecycle stage, not interchangeable synonyms: cancel/void applies before capture (no money moved yet), reversal and refund apply after capture (money returns). Which ones exist, and what each is called, is provider-specific; never auto-substitute one for another or assume all four exist.
controls.applicability: Any code choosing how to undo or return a payment.

source_refs.label: Lifecycle-correct undo operation; provider-specific terms

controls.limitations: Names the lifecycle distinction; the exact operation set and naming must come from the specific provider's docs. cancel/void vs refund/reversal distinction exercised by the refund harness.

controls.statement: Retention is decided per DATA CATEGORY by its legal basis, not globally: mandatory financial/transaction records must be kept for a required minimum; data under an active legal hold must not be deleted even if otherwise erasable; profile/marketing data with no retention obligation is erasable on request. A single blanket retention or deletion rule across all categories is wrong.
controls.applicability: Any data lifecycle, retention schedule, or deletion/erasure feature.

source_refs.label: GDPR Art 17(3)(b) legal-obligation exemption to erasure vs EU AMLD >=5y AML record-keeping; Turkey KVKK (Law 6698) vs Law 5549 retention (jurisdiction-specific)

controls.source_version: GDPR Art 17(3)(b); EU AMLD (>=5y); Turkey Law 5549/KVKK
controls.limitations: Retention is per data category by legal basis, jurisdiction-specific. AML minimum is "at least 5 years" under EU AMLD; some jurisdictions (and Turkey for certain records) require longer. Erasure is not absolute where a legal obligation requires retention (GDPR Art 17(3)(b)).

controls.statement: Over-retention (keeping erasable data past its basis) and over-deletion (erasing data still under a retention obligation or legal hold) are BOTH failures and are checked separately. Crypto-shredding (destroying the key) is an engineering technique, not a universal legal guarantee that the data is 'erased' for every regulator; do not claim it satisfies an erasure duty by itself.
controls.applicability: Any erasure, anonymization, or crypto-shredding implementation.

source_refs.label: Separate over-retention and over-deletion checks; crypto-shredding is not a blanket legal erasure

controls.limitations: Whether crypto-shredding is accepted as erasure is jurisdiction- and regulator-specific; this control forbids presenting it as a universal guarantee. Over-retention and over-deletion checked separately by the retention harness; hold/erase race linearized on real PostgreSQL in CI.

controls.statement: A financial-code review reports per-finding: the FCS control id, file and line, the trigger (what matched), evidence (the actual snippet/reason), a confidence level, and the review's own limits (what it did not or could not check). It reviews the CHANGED risk surface, not only added lines. It never emits an unverified finding as fact and never produces an automatic numeric 'compliance score'; qualitative judgement is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a pass.
controls.applicability: Any automated or assisted review of financial/payment code changes.

source_refs.label: Evidence-bearing per-finding review; no false-precision score

controls.limitations: This is a review discipline, not a scanner: it structures findings and marks uncertainty; it does not certify compliance. Per-finding evidence-bearing review format; qualitative, judged by the review skill rather than an executable test.
